errors.text: The proposed Si addition does not reconstruct the target intervention of 4.2 at.% Cr introduced by vacuum arc melting, and no cited evidence establishes that minor Si will form the required reticulated phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.

The density rationale is chemically incorrect: Si is a low-atomic-mass element, so describing it as having a high atomic mass and predicting that its addition will increase the density of this refractory alloy is unsupported and opposite to the target density trade-off.

The predicted decrease in yield strength conflicts with the target's concurrent strength-ductility improvement, in which Cr-induced lattice contraction and solid-solution hardening raise yield strength while the Laves network improves fracture resistance.
The cited literature generally warns that silicides and continuous grain-boundary intermetallics reduce ambient-temperature ductility; it does not substantiate the claimed beneficial Si-rich network.
